name: evaluate at every field element by multiplying each term by a fixed power
mechanism: to find where a polynomial vanishes over a finite field, keep one register per coefficient; moving from one element to the next multiplies each register by a fixed power of the generator, so every evaluation costs one multiply per term and a sum, and a zero sum marks a root

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Chien search' in section Computational mathematics / Abstract algebra: a recursive algorithm for determining roots of polynomials defined over a finite field

requires: a finite field with a known generator
fails_when: linear in the field size; useless over large fields
